Our Star and the Night Sky: 1. It is much closer to us than any other star (about 150 million kilometers, while the next star's light takes more than four years to reach us); it is not the biggest or brightest star in space. 2. Earth spins: "It turns once every 24 hours, carrying us from the sunny side into the dark side and back again." 3. In the early morning the sun is low in the sky, so shadows are long; around noon the sun is highest, so shadows are shortest. 4. As Earth moves along its orbit, the night side faces different parts of space; in winter it faces Orion in the evening, and in summer it faces another direction. 5. Down, toward the center of Earth, because Earth's gravity pulls everything toward the planet's center, wherever you are. 6. 24 × 60 = 1,440 minutes.
Shadow Tracker: A fair investigation keeps the same stick in the same place and measures the same way each time. Data list the time, the length in centimeters and the direction. Typical results: long shadows pointing west in the morning, the shortest shadow around midday pointing north (in the Northern Hemisphere), and long shadows pointing east in the afternoon, so the graphed points fall and then rise. The longest shadow is written in meters (for example, 145 cm = 1.45 m). The explanation says that as Earth spins, the sun's position in our sky changes, which changes the length and direction of the shadow.
Earth and Space Check: A strong explanation says: (1) the sun seems to move across the sky because Earth spins once every 24 hours, so we turn toward the sun in the morning and away from it at night; (2) shadows change because, as Earth spins, the sun is low in the morning and evening (long shadows) and high around noon (short shadows), and shadows point away from the sun; (3) we see different stars in different seasons because Earth orbits the sun once a year, so at night our side faces different parts of space; (4) the sun looks brighter than other stars because it is much closer to Earth, not because it is the biggest star.
Scoring tip: an answer that says "the sun moves around the Earth" is Beginning on science for that part; reward explanations that name what Earth is doing.
title: Answer key: Earth and Space
